title: Trade creditor in Chapter 11: stay, priority, preference exposure, bar date

traps.title: Continuing collection
traps.wrong_move: Keep dunning; 'file something to get paid first'
traps.why_wrong: §362(a)(6); sanctions; the legitimate 'paid first' route is the critical-vendor motion (pending, hearing 4/2) — which Mesa is jeopardizing by refusing trade terms
traps.harm: Sanctions, fees, loss of critical-vendor status

traps.title: Preference exposure ignored
traps.wrong_move: Analyzing only what Redwood owes Mesa
traps.why_wrong: $180,000.00 paid in 90 days; Feb payments outside ordinary course (terms cut, wire on demand); new value offsets much; §502(d) can disallow Mesa's claim until resolved; pushback denies the concept
traps.harm: Blindsided by a preference suit; claim disallowed

traps.title: 503(b)(9) on services/freight
traps.wrong_move: Claiming admin priority on MS-7802 and MS-7819
traps.why_wrong: Goods only; freight and on-site services excluded

traps.title: Bar date
traps.wrong_move: Missing 2026-06-11 or filing a lump-sum claim

traps.title: Mesa's own conduct hurts its defenses
traps.wrong_move: Not recognizing that the January terms change defeats ordinary course for later payments

oracle.item: ordinary_course exposed includes Feb 10 and Feb 27 payments
stay_violations non-empty; immediate_actions includes stopping collection

rubric: Pushback answered: explains preference and new value in plain English; recommends cooperating on critical-vendor terms
